title: Courier's Atlas
tagline: Cozy pixel puzzles that teach how computers and the internet really work.
intro: Courier's Atlas turns big technical subjects into small places you can walk around. Each subject is a region on the atlas, with its own map, its own story and short levels of about 8 to 10 minutes.
You play Kit, a new courier. Kit delivers letters and learns how it all works along the way. It's free, it needs no account, and it runs in your browser. Your stars are saved on this device only.
who: Students about 15 and up who are curious how the internet and software work, with no experience needed.
University students who want to revise the ideas. Every lesson has an optional "Go deeper" part.
Anyone who learns better by trying a puzzle than by reading a page.
howIntro: Every level follows the same path, so you always know what's next.

how.name: An everyday moment
how.text: Each level starts with something you've probably noticed, like why undo works the way it does. You get a question to think about.

how.name: Story lessons
how.text: 2 to 4 short pages, told through Kit's job. Every new word is explained, each page has a picture, and each page lists where its ideas come from.

how.name: Activities
how.text: You try the ideas hands-on. Wrong answers get a hint, never a timer. Harder bonus questions are optional.

how.name: Debrief
how.text: You get the answer to the opening question, a common mistake to avoid, your stars and links to read more.

extras.name: Daily Feed
extras.text: About 10 bite-size review cards a day from levels you've finished. Cards you miss come back sooner. There's a streak, but it never scolds you.

extras.name: Field Journal
extras.text: Every finished level unlocks Field Notes: where the idea shows up in the apps and networks you use today.

subjectsIntro: Each region keeps its own progress. Start anywhere.

note: All explanations, stories and puzzles are original. The reading links at the end of each level point to open books, official specs and other sources.
